title: The Closed Hand
logline: A family workshop takes on an apprentice from outside the family. The craft passes hand to hand in daily lessons, but some steps are only ever done when the apprentice has gone home.

object.note: Object 3 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: What is held back moves from the catch to a skill: a family workshop that teaches an outsider, but not everything.

thread_out.thread: From a workshop's slow, private tension to an hour of shared heat by a roadside: a broken-down bus and strangers whose mood shifts more than once.

requirements: A hereditary craft workshop currently training an apprentice from outside the family
Consent from the family to show what they are comfortable showing, and no more
An apprentice willing to speak about their own experience of the teaching

suggestions.name: A family brass or metalwork workshop
suggestions.why: A region with a long-standing tradition of hereditary metal-craft workshops, some still family-run and training-based.
suggestions.verify: A specific workshop currently training an outside apprentice must be found and confirmed; this is a region-level suggestion only.
